bihar_raw_news.title: CtrlS datacenters to invest ₹10000 crore in 150 MW AI facility in Bihar
bihar_raw_news.content: CtrlS Datacenters on Friday said it is planning to invest Rs 10,000 crore to set up a 150 MW hyperscale AI facility in Bihar. The company signed a letter of intent with the Bihar government last month for setting up the data centre. “Following the letter of intent signed with the Government of Bihar last month, CtrlS Datacenters has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the state government today to invest Rs 10,000 crore to set up a 150 MW hyperscale AI factory in Bihar,” the company said in a statement. The proposed AI-ready data centre will aim for commercial operations by 2029-30 and will create 400 direct jobs comprising 100 on-site and 300 by hosted customers, the statement said. “The data centre will come up on a 100-acre plot of land located close to a 220/400 kV substation, preferably in or around Patna,” it said. Last month, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary had inaugurated a Rs 400-crore AI and cloud-ready data centre of CtrlS in Patna. Why Bihar's chief secretary has barred bureaucrats from inaugurating projects Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit has directed officials to invite elected representatives to government functions and barred bureaucrats from independently inaugurating development projects, reiterating democratic protocol. Written By Prabhakar Jha Published 21 Nov 2026, 10:41 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Who is Pratyaya Amrit? Why Bihar barred bureaucrats from project inaugurations ( X/@IndustriesBihar ) AI Quick Read Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit has directed government officials to ensure that local MPs, MLAs, MLCs and other elected representatives are invited to inauguration ceremonies, foundation-laying events and other government functions. He has also reiterated that administrative officers should not independently inaugurate development projects or lay their foundation stones, PTI reported. The directive, issued on November 18, follows complaints about bureaucrats allegedly sidelining elected representatives at government functions. It comes amid a controversy in Khagaria, where a Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) MP objected to the exclusion of local legislators from an invitation list for an annual event. Amrit's intervention has brought the relationship between Bihar 's political leadership and its administrative machinery into focus, with the state's top bureaucrat reminding officials that administrative authority does not give them precedence over elected representatives in public functions. Who is Pratyaya Amrit? Pratyaya Amrit is the Chief Secretary of Bihar and the state's highest-ranking administrative official. He oversees the state bureaucracy and plays a key role in coordinating the functioning of government departments and ensuring the implementation of government policies and decisions. In his capacity as Chief Secretary, Amrit is responsible for communicating the state government's administrative directions to senior officials, including additional chief secretaries, principal secretaries, departmental secretaries, divisional commissioners and district magistrates. His latest directive seeks to reinforce the established protocol governing the participation of elected representatives in government programmes and development-related ceremonies. Why has Pratyaya Amrit issued the directive? In a letter dated November 18 addressed to senior bureaucrats and district officials, Amrit expressed concern over instances in which government functions, including inauguration and foundation-laying ceremonies, were conducted without inviting local elected representatives. According to PTI , the Chief Secretary said such practices undermine the dignity of public representatives and go against democratic traditions. He emphasised that Members of Parliament and members of state legislative councils occupy an important position in India's democratic system by virtue of their elected status. Amrit directed officials to ensure that local MPs, MLAs, MLCs and other public representatives are invited to government functions and development-related ceremonies. The India Today report noted that the Chief Secretary also expressed concern that excluding elected representatives could create the impression among people that their representatives were not being given due importance, potentially weakening public confidence in them. The directive further reiterates earlier instructions issued by the Cabinet Secretariat Department, which stated that administrative officers should not independently inaugurate development projects or lay their foundation stones. On the occasion, he also inaugurated and laid the foundation stones of development projects worth over 34,000 crore rupees. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister highlighted Bihar’s development journey, good governance and various welfare initiatives. The Prime Minister Narendra Modi was accorded a traditional welcome with a stole adorned with Bajjika artwork, flowers made of makhana, a garland of Aparajita flowers and bananas. Following the welcome, the Prime Minister dedicated the six-lane Nitish Setu, built across the River Ganga, to the people of Bihar. Stretching approximately 20 kilometres, the bridge connects Kachchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali district. With the inauguration of this bridge, traffic pressure on the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu is expected to ease, while connectivity between North and South Bihar will become smoother. The Prime Minister said that the bridge has been named in honour of former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. He described it as a symbol of his service and dedication to Bihar. Describing Nitish Setu as more than just a means of transportation, the Prime Minister said that the project would make people’s daily lives easier. He added that it would help local products reach larger markets and improve access to education and healthcare services. In his address, the Prime Minister invoked the blessings of Chhathi Maiya and said that Bihar was celebrating a festival of development. He recalled that three decades ago, the people of Bihar had chosen the path of hope and faith, and that under the leadership of Nitish Kumar, the state had gained renewed confidence in good governance. During the programme, the Prime Minister presented a total of 227 development projects to the state. These include the second 660-megawatt unit of the Buxar Thermal Power Project, along with several initiatives related to road construction, power distribution and transmission, irrigation, education, healthcare and urban development. The Prime Minister also flagged off 100 electric buses under the PM-e-Bus initiative and participated in the Griha Pravesh ceremony for more than 26 900 beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban. Now, the state of Bihar has added another major milestone to its infrastructure map with the inauguration of Nitish Setu, a six-lane bridge across the River Ganga that will transform connectivity between North and South Bihar. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the ambitious project in Vaishali district on Saturday, November 21, 2026, marking a significant moment in the state’s infrastructure development. Named after former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, built at an estimated cost of ₹4,280 crore, the 9.76-kilometre-long main bridge is part of a larger 19.7 kilometre connectivity corridor, including approximately 10 kilometres of approach roads. The project connects Kachhi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali district, linking National Highway 22 with NH-322. More importantly, it provides an additional crossing over the Ganga, reducing the pressure on existing bridges, particularly the heavily used Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu. The significance of Nitish Setu goes well beyond reducing traffic congestion. For residents of Raghopur Diara, improved connectivity means easier access to hospitals, educational institutions, government services and employment opportunities in Patna. Areas that have historically struggled with transportation challenges will now have a more dependable road connection. The economic implications are significant. Faster movement of agricultural produce, industrial goods and commercial vehicles can improve market access, reduce transportation delays, and encourage investment. Better connectivity is often the foundation upon which industrial development, logistics networks and new economic opportunities emerge. The bridge also represents an important example of how large infrastructure projects can change the economic geography of a state. Bihar has considerable potential in agriculture, trade and manufacturing, but inadequate connectivity has historically remained a major obstacle. Nitish Setu is therefore more than another bridge across the Ganga. It is an investment in Bihar’s economic future, bringing communities closer to opportunities and making transportation more efficient. As India continues to invest in highways, expressways, railways and modern bridges, Bihar’s infrastructure transformation is an important part of the larger national development story. For the people of Bihar, the real success of Nitish Setu will ultimately be measured not merely in kilometres of concrete and steel, but in the opportunities it creates for generations to come. national_raw_news.content: The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) opened in Goa on Friday, with a spectacular inaugural ceremony at Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Stadium, bringing together filmmakers, film personalities and cinema enthusiasts from across the world. With more than 150 films from 86 countries, this year’s festival is being held under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, celebrating cinema’s ability to transcend geographical boundaries, bridge cultural differences and connect audiences through shared human emotions. Set against the backdrop of Goa’s cultural and coastal landscape, the nine-day festival aims to provide an international platform for diverse cinematic voices, creative exchange and collaboration. The inaugural ceremony featured prominent political leaders, government officials, filmmakers and artists, while international musical performances added to the celebrations. Goa aims to become a comprehensive filmmaking hub: Pramod Sawant Addressing the gathering, Goa Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant said IFFI had become an integral part of the state’s cultural calendar over the past 22 years. He noted that the festival celebrates cinema’s ability to bring different cultures together and linked this year’s theme to India’s timeless philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — the world is one family. “Cinema allows us to experience different cultures and find the common ground that unites us,” he said. Highlighting the inclusion of Ramayana in the BRICS Cinema section, Sawant described it as a proud moment for India. He also underlined IFFI’s role in promoting Indian cinema, particularly Marathi, Konkani and Goan films, and expressed hope that the festival would encourage more young people from Goa to take up filmmaking and present their stories to national and international audiences. Outlining the state’s ambition to develop a comprehensive filmmaking ecosystem, the Chief Minister said, “We want Goa to be the destination where films are produced and completed.” He highlighted the Goa Film Shooting Act, 2021, the online single-window clearance system and financial assistance schemes for filmmakers as key measures to strengthen the state’s film industry. He also announced a vision to establish a film city equipped with pre-production and post-production facilities, visual effects (VFX) infrastructure and film education facilities. Sawant said advancements in animation, artificial intelligence and virtual production were creating new opportunities for the film industry. Goa, he added, aims to equip its young creative talent to participate in the rapidly evolving global filmmaking landscape. national_raw_news.title: 57th IFFI showcases 12 Goan films, bringing Konkani and Marathi stories to global audiences
national_raw_news.content: Twelve films in Konkani and Marathi will bring the stories, people and cultural experiences of Goa to an international audience at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), offering a cinematic exploration of the state’s social realities, traditions and everyday lives. The specially curated Goan film package, scheduled to be screened at INOX Panjim from November 21 to 28, 2026, features a mix of feature films and short films. The selection explores themes such as identity, family relationships, personal struggles, childhood, loneliness and self-discovery, presenting narratives that are rooted in local experiences but carry universal emotional appeal. From an elderly woman confronting her conscience and a forgotten local hero revisiting his past to a daughter seeking reconciliation with her family and an old villager defending his ancestral home, the films cover a wide range of human experiences. The collection also includes comedies and dramas that examine changing social relationships and the complexities of everyday life. Stories of identity, family and personal discovery Among the Konkani films, Manguirish J. Bandodkar’s 30-minute Ancessao follows an elderly woman living alone in a quiet Goan village. She fills the silence of her life by talking about others but eventually realises that her gossip is a way of avoiding her own unresolved grief. Prompted by her conscience, she resolves to change her behaviour, although the transformation proves short-lived. Vardhan Vijaykumar Kamat’s Umesh, a 99-minute Konkani film, explores identity, trust and the consequences of a forgotten legacy. It follows a once-celebrated local hero who now lives in isolation in a rural village, surviving on odd jobs and carrying the burden of an unresolved past. His circumstances change when aspiring filmmakers Anton and Rohan arrive to document his life. Their investigation into local rumours and half-truths gradually reveals his forgotten talent and the painful reasons behind his withdrawal from society. As a relationship of trust develops, Umesh becomes increasingly uncomfortable with the camera. Family ties, tradition and reconciliation form the core of Prasad M. Naik’s 11-minute film Shakuntala. The story follows a woman who becomes estranged from her conservative family after marrying a Christian man from her neighbourhood. Years later, after her father’s death, she is denied the opportunity to attend his funeral. As the twelfth-day death ritual approaches, she gathers the courage to return to her childhood home, confronting long-buried conflicts and social judgment in an effort to reclaim her place as a daughter. Shravan Kankonkar’s 25-minute Purnata takes a different approach to the continuity of life through the journey of Zayo, a garland of jasmine flowers. As the garland passes through different hands, it brings comfort, hope and happiness during moments of joy and sorrow. Even as the flowers wither, they continue to touch lives, reflecting on how purpose and life carry forward even when one journey comes to an end. Relationships, memories and the challenges of growing up Suvidha Torgal Bakhle’s 16-minute Konkani film Noise examines human behaviour and recurring patterns in relationships. Its central character, Tara, struggles to move away from a troubled relationship but repeatedly finds herself drawn towards familiar patterns despite her efforts to heal. The recurring presence of an old fan serves as a metaphor for these cycles and the difficulty of changing behaviour even when the need for change is recognised. In the Marathi film Daryaa, directed by Kishor Arjun, a 25-minute narrative explores the experience of discovering the world through imagination and senses beyond sight. The story follows Aakash, a visually impaired boy with cerebral palsy who has never seen the sea and knows it only through stories, sounds and imagination. When his grandfather takes him on an unexpected journey to the coast, Aakash encounters the place he has long dreamed of visiting. The film reflects on the meaning of seeing and the ways people experience the world. Sankalp Sainath Parab’s 14-minute Konkani film Perfect Shot follows Vasudha, a young film school student whose pursuit of the perfect cinematic frame becomes an obsession with the Golden Ratio, symmetry and the rule of thirds. At the same time, she struggles with unresolved feelings towards her late father, believing he left her with nothing of value. national_raw_news.content: PM to visit West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November | Prime Minister of India News Updates PM to visit West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November 20 Nov, 2026 PM to participate in Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur PM to participate in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow 52 national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes, National Skill Training Institutes and Institutes for Training of Trainers to be felicitated for outstanding achievements Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November 2026. IIT Kharagpur, established in 1951, was the first Indian Institute of Technology to be set up in the country. Top Stories of the Day Share DD India November 21, 2026 1:17 AM IST Indian Navy | Diving Support Craft | DSC A21 Indian Navy receives indigenously built diving support craft DSC A21 in Mumbai Author: DD India The Indian Navy on Friday received DSC A21, the latest vessel under its Diving Support Craft (DSC) project, at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. The vessel has been indigenously designed and constructed by Kolkata-based Titagarh Rail Systems Limited (TRSL). Featuring a catamaran-hull design, DSC A21 is equipped with state-of-the-art diving equipment and specialised systems to support the Navy’s underwater operations. Its design provides enhanced stability, an enlarged deck area and improved sea-keeping characteristics, making it suitable for its specialised operational role. Indigenous design and construction The vessel has been designed and built indigenously in accordance with the relevant Naval Rules and Regulations of the Indian Register of Shipping (IRS). The Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL), Visakhapatnam, undertook hydrodynamic analysis and model testing during the design stage. With the induction of vessels under the project, the Indian Navy’s capabilities in diving support, underwater inspection, salvage assistance and coastal operational deployment are set to receive a boost. DSC A21 also represents the government’s Make in India initiative in the defence sector, highlighting the contribution of domestic industry to the design and construction of specialised naval platforms. national_raw_news.content: India's critical mineral push securing mineral supplies through both domestic and overseas sources: Ministry of Mines Secretary Keshav Chandra Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर India's critical mineral push securing mineral supplies through both domestic and overseas sources: Ministry of Mines Secretary Keshav Chandra ANI | Updated: Nov 21, 2026 07:46 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 21 (ANI): Ministry of Mines Secretary Keshav Chandra highlighted the Ministry's reform agenda to enhance the sector's global competitiveness through geological exploration, responsible mining, advanced processing, research, recycling and technology-enabled governance. Speaking at the Ministry of Mines-FICCI closed-door industry interaction, he also outlined recent auction reforms, including relaxation of minimum bidder requirements for certain minerals and automatic issuance of Letters of Intent. Responding comprehensively to the concerns raised by the industry, Chandra apprised participants of the various initiatives and measures already undertaken or under consideration by the Ministry. He addressed operational challenges relating to mineral block development. He urged the industry to actively consider extraction of critical minerals from resources such as red mud. The interaction also witnessed the launch of a concept paper, Enabling Overseas Investment in Critical Minerals: Policy, Financial and Institutional Framework for Securing India's Critical Mineral Supply Chains. Chandra emphasised that to secure mineral supplies, opportunities are being explored both at the domestic and overseas levels. He observed that the paper's emphasis on moving from MoUs to project delivery aligns with the Ministry's efforts, including KABIL's overseas engagements, and expressed interest in examining its recommendations. On overseas critical mineral investments, he discussed the importance of enabling mechanisms to improve project viability. He emphasised the Ministry's continued efforts to address industry concerns through policy and regulatory reforms, institutional coordination and targeted interventions, while encouraging industry to actively participate in strengthening India's domestic and overseas mineral supply chains. Opening the interaction, Pankaj Satija, Co-Chair, FICCI Mining Committee and Executive VP, JSW, appreciated the Ministry's reforms in exploration, mineral auctions and mine operationalisation. He highlighted growing global supply chain vulnerabilities arising from export controls, domestic value-addition requirements and processing technology restrictions, underscoring the importance of diversified and resilient mineral supply chains for India's industrial and economic security. FICCI noted that the concept paper, prepared pursuant to the mandate received from the Ministry of Mines, draws on extensive research and stakeholder consultations to identify barriers to overseas mineral investments and propose actionable solutions. The paper also presents a Country-Priority Mineral Matrix to guide strategic overseas investments and proposes a tiered framework for prioritising projects for government facilitation. It emphasises stronger institutional coordination, streamlined approvals and integration of overseas mineral investments with domestic processing and manufacturing capabilities to translate international partnerships into assured mineral supplies for India. Under the guidance of Kadam Sandeep Vasant, Joint Secretary and Head, National Critical Mineral Mission, Ministry of Mines, the paper has been authored by Arpan Gupta, Director, FICCI and Siddhant Chandra, Assistant Director, FICCI.
